And Joseph was not able to control himself before all who stood by him, and he called out, "Have every man go out from me!" And no man stood with him when Joseph made himself known to his brothers.
And he let out his voice in weeping, and Egypt heard, and Pharaoh's house heard.
And Joseph said to his brothers, "I am Joseph. Is my father still alive?" And his brothers were not able to answer him, for they were dismayed before him.
And Joseph said to his brothers, "Come close to me, please." And they came close. And he said, "I am Joseph your brother, whom you sold into Egypt.
And now, do not be pained, and let there be no anger in your eyes that you sold me here, for it was to preserve life that God sent me ahead of you.
For these two years the famine has been in the midst of the land, and there are five more years in which there will be no plowing or harvest.
And God sent me ahead of you to set a remnant for you on the earth, and to keep you alive as a great company of survivors [alt: by a great deliverance].
And now, it was not you who sent me here, but God, and he has made me a father to Pharaoh, and lord of all his house, and the one who governs all the land of Egypt.
Hurry and go up to my father and say to him, 'This is what your son Joseph says: God has made me lord of all Egypt. Come down to me; do not delay.
And you will live in the land of Goshen, and you will be near me, you and your sons and your sons' sons, and your flocks and your cattle and all that you have.
And I will provide for you there, for there are five more years of famine, so that you do not come to poverty, you and your household and all that you have.'
And look, your eyes see, and the eyes of my brother Benjamin, that it is my mouth that is speaking to you.
And you are to tell my father of all my honor in Egypt and of all that you have seen, and you are to hurry and bring my father down here."
And he fell on the neck of Benjamin his brother and wept, and Benjamin wept on his neck.
And he kissed all his brothers and wept on them, and afterward his brothers spoke with him.
And the news was heard in Pharaoh's house, saying, "Joseph's brothers have come," and it was good in the eyes of Pharaoh and in the eyes of his servants.
And Pharaoh said to Joseph, "Say to your brothers, 'Do this: load your animals and go, enter the land of Canaan,
and take your father and your households and come to me, and let me give you the good things of the land of Egypt, and eat the fat of the land.'
And as for you, you are commanded: 'Do this: take wagons for yourselves from the land of Egypt for your little ones and for your wives, and carry your father and come.
And do not look with regret on your things, for the good things of all the land of Egypt are yours.'"
And the sons of Israel did so, and Joseph gave them wagons according to the word of Pharaoh, and he gave them provisions for the way.
To all of them he gave, to each man, changes of clothes, and to Benjamin he gave three hundred pieces of silver and five changes of clothes.
And to his father he sent as follows: ten donkeys carrying some of the good things of Egypt, and ten female donkeys carrying grain and bread and food for his father for the way.
And he sent his brothers on their way, and they went, and he said to them, "Do not get angry on the way [alt: Do not be afraid on the way]."
And they went up from Egypt and came to the land of Canaan, to Jacob their father.
And they told him, saying, "Joseph is still alive," and that he was the one governing all the land of Egypt. And his heart went numb, for he did not believe them.
And they spoke to him all the words of Joseph that he had spoken to them, and he saw the wagons that Joseph had sent to carry him, and the spirit of Jacob their father revived.
And Israel said, "Enough! Joseph my son is still alive. Let me go and see him before I die."
